newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to sell Ajkai alumina plant.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to sell Ajkai alumina plant.

text.p: Hungary's privatization agency APV Rt will offer a 90 percent stake in Ajkai Aluminiumipari Kft, APV said on Wednesday.
"The stake worth a nominal 1.59 billion forints will be offered in a one-round public tender," APV said in a statement.

It added that plans for long-term operation of the plant, environmental improvements, necessary investments, the use of domestic bauxite and maintaining the present workforce will be important evaluation criteria.
The remaining 10 percent stake will be set aside for employees, APV said.
Norwegian energy giant Norsk Hydro said in June it wants to buy Ajkai, Hungary's biggest alumina plant, and intends to use it to supply the Slovak aluminium smelter (Slovalco) it partly owns.

If it got Ajka, Norsk Hydro would invest $15 million to boost capacity to 330,000 tonnes a year and to replace flour- grade and special alumina production with sandy-grade alumina, a Hydro Hungary official said in June.

Ajka's current capacity is 300,000 tonnes of alumina a year, and it currently produces 65,000 tonnes a year of flour-grade smelter alumina, 35,000 tonnes of zeolites and dry hydrates and 100,000 tonnes of special alumina and hydrates.

In addition to alumina, Ajka also produces gallium out of bauxite. Current production is five tonnes a year, roughly a tenth of the world output of the metal that is used in electronics and the space industry.
